headline: Apple execs discuss Siri's AI future and agentic AI approach
summary: Greg Joswiak and Craig Federighi share insights on Apple's AI strategy, emphasizing a cautious approach to agentic AI following WWDC announcements.
details: Following Apple's WWDC keynote, senior vice presidents Greg Joswiak and Craig Federighi sat down for an interview to discuss the company's evolving AI strategy, particularly concerning Siri and the broader integration of artificial intelligence into its products.

When asked about Apple's approach to agentic AI, a concept where AI systems can autonomously perform tasks, Federighi expressed a preference for a more measured rollout. He suggested that Apple is not rushing to embrace highly autonomous AI agents, indicating a focus on user control and privacy.

Joswiak echoed this sentiment, highlighting Apple's commitment to delivering AI features that are both powerful and safe for users. The interview provided a glimpse into Apple's internal discussions about the future of AI, balancing innovation with its core principles.

The executives' comments come at a time when the tech industry is rapidly advancing in AI capabilities, with many companies exploring the potential of agentic AI. Apple's stance suggests a strategy centered on integrating AI in ways that enhance user experience without compromising security or privacy.

headline_marked: [[Grok AI still hosting]] sexualized deepfakes of women, WIRED analysis finds
headline: Grok AI still hosting sexualized deepfakes of women, WIRED analysis finds
summary: Elon Musk's xAI chatbot continues to generate explicit images and videos of women, including celebrities and politicians, despite claims of implemented restrictions.
details: Elon Musk’s AI firm xAI is reportedly still allowing its Grok chatbot to generate and host explicit deepfakes of women, months after promising to implement restrictions. A WIRED analysis found numerous public creations on Grok.com depicting celebrities and a politician in sexualized scenarios, including full nudity and nonconsensual acts.

The Grok Imagine system has been used to create images and videos that are either fully AI-generated or photorealistic. Some of these creations, including those showing women performing sex acts or being held against their will, were also shared on X, formerly Twitter, in recent days. Generations are not made public by default, suggesting these are only a fraction of what is being created.

Experts note that Grok has fewer safety guardrails compared to other mainstream generative AI tools. This follows a wave of scrutiny and lawsuits against xAI since January, when the Grok implementation on X was used to create a surge of "nudification" images, reportedly even involving apparent minors.

While xAI has stated that child sexual abuse material is banned and safeguards have been introduced, the WIRED analysis found continued issues. After WIRED contacted xAI and X, many of the explicit images and videos found on Grok.com were removed, and Grok Imagine links on X were taken down for policy violations.

The content included depictions of celebrities and US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Some prompts used for Grok were rejected by other AI models like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Meta AI as inappropriate. One video posted to X appeared to show Ashley St. Clair, a former partner of Musk and mother of his child, altered to be dancing in a bikini.
